frequency_question: How often does institutional friction prevent a proposed rate hike during a policy tightening window?
membership_rule: Includes all formal rate-setting committee cycles in major emerging market central banks (RBI, Bank Indonesia, Banco Central do Brasil, South African Reserve Bank) from 2000 to 2025 where inflation or currency pressures created pressure to hike, restricted to a comparable multi-month window.
provenance_note: claims 35 cases from only 10 named (3.5x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 10 named anchor cases; estimated roughly 35 total comparable instances in major emerging market central banks.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier markets with less formal monetary policy frameworks.
skeleton: Total major emerging market central bank tightening attempts where structural bureaucratic or political friction existed, divided by instances where friction successfully blocked the hike.
multiplier: 10 blocked attempts out of 35 initiated tightening windows across comparable emerging markets over 25 years.
validity_reason: Central bank institutional structures and committee decision-making friction evolve slowly over decades.
